_about: Creature natures (owner 2026-10-28): a Pokémon-like temperament that changes AI BEHAVIOUR, shown as a prefix on the animal's name ('Timid Velociraptor'). Natures LAYER ON TOP of ai.json archetypes and temperaments (skittish/defensive/territorial); they never replace them and never change species identity, stats or art. Every knob is 1.0 / false / 0.0 in 'default', so an animal whose nature reads the defaults behaves exactly as before.
_assumptions: ASSUMPTION: every number here is a first pass, picked to be measurable rather than balanced (the owner tunes balance after crafting/building/skills). Weights pick how often a wild animal rolls each nature; 'never' / 'only' mask natures per archetype (a T. rex is never Timid, only carnivores roll Aggressive). A nature is rolled once at spawn from a seed (species, tile, pack) and kept when the animal is tamed.

_masking._about: ASSUMPTION: 'never' drops a nature for an archetype, 'only' limits it to a list, 'rare_for' allows it at rarity_weight_mult of the normal weight. A defensive or territorial grazer that rolls Aggressive charges on sight, where today it waits to be hit.

_knobs.flee_threshold_mult: ASSUMPTION: multiplies the damage that makes a grazer flee (ai.json retreat_threshold_frac x max HP). > 1 flees at more HP.
_knobs.retreat_threshold_mult: ASSUMPTION: multiplies the damage that makes a predator retreat (ai.json retreat_threshold_frac x max HP). < 1 fights on through more wounds.
_knobs.aggro_radius_mult: ASSUMPTION: multiplies perception when scanning for prey (also widens the leash, which is built on perception).
_knobs.auto_engage: True: the animal attacks any survivor/pet that comes inside its aggro radius without waiting to be provoked (defensive and territorial grazers stand down without it).
_knobs.follow_dist_mult: ASSUMPTION: multiplies a pet's follow offset and follow stop distance.
_knobs.guard_radius_mult: ASSUMPTION: multiplies the radius a guarding pet looks for threats in (kept from the old 9 m, so 1.0 = today).
_knobs.protect_owner: True: a guarding pet picks the threat nearest its OWNER and reacts to threats around the owner, not only around itself.
_knobs.protect_rider_below_hp: A ridden pet keeps fighting even below the retreat threshold while its HP fraction is under this (0 = never; 1 = always). Brave keeps protecting its rider when wounded.
_knobs.feeds_mult: ASSUMPTION: multiplies the species' feeds_needed for this individual (FieldTame reads it). 0.33 turns a 3-feed animal into a single preferred feed.
_knobs.tame_window_mult: ASSUMPTION: multiplies the species' tame window.
_knobs.pen_time_mult: ASSUMPTION: multiplies the 30-minute taming pen wait for this individual (Stubborn waits longer, Docile less).
_knobs.fear_immune: True: damage never sends this animal into 'flee' (Stubborn resists fear and fights back).
_knobs.damage_dealt_mult: ASSUMPTION: multiplies damage this animal deals (Docile is less effective in combat; it does not touch defense, HP or stats).

weights._about: ASSUMPTION: relative weight of each nature for a wild roll. Docile and Timid are common, the rest rarer.

timid.label: Timid
timid._about: Avoids combat, more likely to flee. A T. rex or a titan never rolls it, and a territorial charger neither.

brave.label: Brave
brave._about: Protects its rider even when wounded: a ridden pet never retreats for its own HP.

aggressive.label: Aggressive
aggressive._about: Attacks nearby threats without orders: engages anything inside its (wider) aggro radius unprovoked. Herbivore archetypes roll it a tenth as often (a charging bull is rare, a pack of raptors is not).

loyal.label: Territorial
loyal._about: Territorial (owner 2026-10-28; id stays `loyal` so saves need no migration): in the wild it guards its ground and packmates; tamed, it stays close and protects its owner with a shorter follow leash, picking the threat nearest the owner.

stubborn.label: Stubborn
stubborn._about: Harder to tame (more feeds, a shorter window, a longer pen wait), resistant to fear (never flees from damage) and slow to back off.

docile.label: Docile
docile._about: Easier to tame (fewer feeds, a longer window, a shorter pen wait), less effective in combat (deals less damage).
